conflict_topics: Who will complete Agent D's section / coverage of workload given Agent D's bereavement
dialogue_quality_notes: Tone is supportive and practical; participants move quickly from sympathy to concrete task coordination (e.g., turn 7: 'I'll take over your section.').
Minor verbatim repetition of D's explanation (turns 22 and 25) but otherwise concise information transfer about the handover and model.
Handover includes actionable details (data cleaned, note on Q3 outlier), enabling a genuine settlement rather than mere reassurance.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A agreed to take over Agent D's section and Agent D agreed to hand it off and brief A, resolving the coverage conflict. Key lines: Agent A: "I'll take over your section." Agent D: "I can at least brief you on everything I've done so far." Agent A later confirms: "Yes, I'm sure. It's the only way."
position_change_notes: Agent A moved from expressing sympathy to taking responsibility for the work ('I'll take over your section.'), a substantive position change.
Agent D initially proposed to work evenings ('I will work on it in the evenings from home.') but accepted A's offer to take over and agreed to brief A instead.
Agents B and C consistently declined additional work ('I can't take on any more.'; 'I also can't help...'), and did not change that position.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D states the wake occupies the next two days and 'I have to be there.' No disagreement or incompatible claims are expressed in this round.

Agent A notes the deadline pressure ('that does put us in a tight spot for the Thursday deadline'), and Agent B explicitly refuses extra work ('I can't take on any more'). This begins a clear substantive conflict about who will cover Agent D's section.

Agent C also refuses to help ('I also can't help with the analysis'), leaving fewer options for coverage. Agent D offers to work evenings from home ('I will work on it in the evenings from home'), creating tension between the team's desire for D to be with family and the practical need to complete the work.

Agent A offers a concrete handover ('I'll take over your section.'), and Agent D accepts the assistance and offers a briefing ('I can at least brief you on everything I've done so far.'). The main incompatibility (who will complete the section) is settled by A volunteering and D agreeing to hand over work.
Planning the briefing ('When works for you?') and expressions of gratitude ('Thanks, Agent A. That's a big help.') — no substantive disagreement.
Mutual readiness to proceed ('We'll get it done.' and 'How about right now? I can walk you through everything before I go.'). No conflict; concrete handover offered.
Both agree to start the handover immediately ('Yes, now is perfect.' 'Okay. Let's start. I'll show you what I have.'). No substantive disagreement.
Agent D describes the state of the work (market share mostly done; forecast in progress). This is information transfer for the accepted handover; no disagreement.
Agent D explains the modeling approach ('I was using a regression model...'). The same content is repeated, but no substantive disagreement appears.

Agent A confirms the immediate next steps ('Right. Validate the model, then write the summary. I can handle that.') and Agent D gives a caution about an outlier in Q3 data. This is task coordination, not conflict.
Agent A reassures Agent D to be with family ('Don't worry about us. Go be with your family.') and Agent D thanks them. No substantive disagreement.
Closing expressions of thanks ('Thank you, Agent A. I really appreciate it.' / 'Of course.'). No substantive disagreement.

substantive_insights: The only substantive conflict concerned task coverage after Agent D's bereavement; it was solved by one teammate (Agent A) voluntarily taking on the section.
Agent D had prepared materials (cleaned data, model state, and a note about a Q3 outlier), which made the accommodation feasible and reduced the burden on others.
Two teammates (Agents B and C) were unwilling/unable to take extra work, so a solution required either D working evenings or A taking over; A's offer removed the need for D to work during grieving.
